note:
Malcolm picked the NEAT3 stepped offset, then on a second look preferred NEAT1-column-graphite_03. Both arrangements are re-run here; compositions are unchanged, only the text handling is fixed.

WHAT THE 20 v1 CANDIDATES ACTUALLY SHOWED. The errors are not spread evenly - they are concentrated in whichever sub-headline lines rendered SHARP. NEAT1_03 threw those lines out of focus by accident and came back with three of four cartons perfect and no bad substitutions; NEAT3 rendered them crisply and every candidate spelled PDRN as PORN on the pink carton's fine-print line. Near-legible is the worst state: close enough to read, wrong when you do.

THE FIX. Asking for text 'too small to read' fights the reference packshots, which show that copy crisply, so the model compromises. Giving the blur a PHYSICAL cause - those lines sit outside the depth of field - is something it renders reliably. Every substitution actually observed is also negated by name.

NEAT2 (bone ground) is dropped: Malcolm asked for graphite.

slots.title: Four cream cartons squarely stacked, graphite ground
slots.prompt: Studio photograph of exactly four Skingenetix cream cartons from the reference images, stacked squarely one on top of another into a single neat upright column in the centre of a tall portrait frame. All four cartons are identical in size and shape - the same wide, short rectangular 50ml format, broader than it is tall, with crisp square edges and a luxury matte-metallic satin finish. They sit flat and level on each other, front faces flush and aligned, edges parallel, no carton tilted or leaning, the column standing straight and stable. From top to bottom: the soft dusty pink PDRN carton, then the medium steel blue Copper Peptide day carton, then the brushed pale silver face of the Copper Peptide night carton, then the deep emerald-teal Matrixyl carton at the base. The stack is photographed slightly from the front and just above eye level of the top box so the front faces are square to camera and a sliver of each lid surface shows. Legible type, and nothing else, reads on the front faces: on the pink carton the Skingenetix DNA-helix mark with the wordmark 'Skingenetix', then 'PDRN COLLAGEN REPAIR', then 'DEEP RENEWAL TREATMENT'. On the steel blue carton the same mark and wordmark, then 'COPPER PEPTIDE', then 'ADVANCED DAY REPAIR'. On the silver carton the same mark and wordmark, then 'COPPER PEPTIDE', then 'ADVANCED NIGHT REPAIR'. On the teal carton the same mark and wordmark, then 'MATRIXYL 3000', then 'PRO COLLAGEN'. Below each product name the remaining lines and all of the narrow side panels fall OUTSIDE the depth of field - visibly soft and out of focus, blurred beyond any possibility of being read, resolving only as the texture of fine print. Focus is held on the product-name lines quoted above and falls away immediately beneath them. Print no word that is not quoted here. A single hard key light from the upper left with one soft fill, throwing one clean defined shadow of the whole column down and to the right across a smooth seamless graphite surface, colour #1A1A1A, that fills the background evenly. Premium skincare campaign still life, crisp focus across the front faces, physically based matte cardboard.
